rationale: New obligation and its first check for a codec contract break found while reviewing the durable record's use of the same value codec: the value length is a 16-bit field, the client's command size is configuration-driven, and an oversized value is silently shortened on the wire while its remaining bytes stay in the stream. The harness round-trips one 70000-byte value through the real codec and observes 4464 decoded bytes with only 4477 consumed; the trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide it. The consequence is bounded because the shipped configuration uses 1000-byte commands.

candidate.rationale: The obligation and binding are supplied with the check so the claim exists before the plan references it; the duty is that a value the client can build survives the codec.

question.question: A command value of 70000 bytes is marshalled and unmarshalled through the implementation's own codec. Does the value survive unchanged, or does the two-byte length field store it modulo 65536 so the decoder recovers a shorter value and leaves the rest of the bytes in the stream?
question.importance: The client command size is configuration-driven, so a value beyond the length field range is constructible; a silent truncation both shortens the command a replica may apply and shifts every following message boundary on that reader, turning a configuration choice into corrupted replication input and reader desynchronisation. The consequence is bounded in the default deployment because aws.conf sets 1000-byte commands.
contexts: client command size is a configuration value
event_paths: the command is marshalled, writing a two-byte value length
the decoded length and consumed bytes are compared with what was written

supporting_behavior_ids.B15-durable-record: another consumer of the same value codec, which shows the codec is used wherever commands are written
supporting_behavior_ids.B16-client-reply: the consumer that answers the client whose command carries the value

counterevidence: scoped to the source: the value codec writes the length with a 16-bit field on both sides, so a larger value is stored modulo 65536 while all of its bytes are emitted (S37-state-value-codec)
scoped to the run: the local construction run reports declared 70000 bytes, wire 70013 bytes, decoded 4464 bytes and 4477 bytes consumed, with value_matches false
scoped to the default deployment: aws.conf sets commandSize 1000, so the shipped configuration never reaches the truncation (S38-client-command-size)
unknowns: whether the client library caps the command size it builds
what a replica reader does on the following message once the stream is shifted, which no check exercised
question.trigger_rationale: The A1 relationship is the command value entering decision formation: B11-prepare-resolution carries the recovered value back into the accept and commit path, and the committed decision it produces is F2, whose content is the command bytes the codec framed. The question asks whether a value the client's configuration permits can reach that path at all, or whether the codec shortens it and shifts the stream.

obligation.description: The command codec must carry the value length the client's configured command size permits: a command value that the client can build must either survive a marshal/unmarshal round trip unchanged or be rejected, never silently shortened.

scope.description: One command with a value of 70000 bytes marshalled and unmarshalled through the real codec, on a deployment whose client command size is configurable (aws.conf sets 1000).
assumptions: the client's command size is a configuration value, so larger values are constructible
the codec is the only framing between a client or peer and the replica's readers
excluded: the default deployment's 1000-byte commands, which are inside the field's range
what a replica does after its reader desynchronises on the following message

grounding.derivation: The value codec writes the length into a two-byte field, so any value larger than 65535 bytes is stored modulo 65536 while its bytes are still emitted. The decoder trusts that length, reads fewer bytes than were written and leaves the remainder in the stream, which both shortens the command and shifts every following message boundary.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any caller whose command value can exceed 65535 bytes, which the configuration allows by construction; the shipped configuration sets 1000, so the duty is owed by the codec rather than violated in the default deployment.
unresolved: whether the client refuses oversized commands before sending (client/buffer.go allocates the configured size, which the read did not check for a cap)

associations.rationale: Both sides of the codec read and write the length through a 16-bit field, which is what truncates a larger value.

bindings.description: Value wire codec: a two-byte length prefix in Marshal and the same field in Unmarshal.
